minutes.headline: Sewer Commission set a Dec 5 hearing on Crossroads' overdue fees and asked staff for a spare-parts update.
minutes.summary: The commission heard the schools' facilities director on reopening the Paseos kitchen for two small food businesses and what grease trap cleaning, permits and waivers would apply. It then covered DPW updates (manhole task one, small water spare parts, task two I&I), the 380 Electric Ave privilege fee, billing outsourcing, and Crossroads' overdue fees. A hearing was moved to December 5 and the 28th meeting rescheduled.

what_happened.line: The commission moved to call a hearing for Crossroads on overdue non-compliance fees, aiming for the December 5 meeting; the vote count was not stated.
The letter to Crossroads is to go out by about Nov 12, and a draft goes to commissioners first.
A motion directed staff to email an update within a week on small water and the spare parts situation; the count was not stated.
The commission heard the schools' facilities director on reopening the Paseos kitchen; applicants are to handle the permit and gather data for a later grease trap waiver request.
Only one December meeting will be held, on December 5, in place of Nov 28 and Dec 12.

why_it_matters: Overdue sewer fees that go unpaid can end in a lien or a pulled sewer permit, so how the commission handles Crossroads affects how consistently fees are enforced on all sewer users.
Grease trap cleaning costs and permit fees could decide whether small food businesses can operate in the Paseos kitchen, which is a school-owned space.
watch_next: December 5 meeting: the hearing on Crossroads' non-compliance fees, with the letter due out by about Nov 12.
Next meeting agenda: small water spare parts, 380 Electric Ave privilege fee, task one status, task two information, and the Oct 10 minutes.
